subject: SIG Q23 — Data residency: interpretation for retained vs. transient artifacts
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@usmartbank.com>, Megan Liu <megan.liu@usmartbank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SIG Q23 — Data residency: interpretation for retained vs. transient artifacts

Hi Jordan / Megan,

Thanks for sending over the SIG spreadsheet — we're working through the rows. Q23 ("Are logs, backups, or cached data containing customer data retained outside the region specified by the contract?") reads a bit broadly and customers have differed on whether "retained" covers short-lived in-memory and cache artifacts. Before we complete the spreadsheet we'd like to confirm Redwood's intended interpretation so we don't create work for your reviewers.

Proposed Redwood interpretation (high level):
- "Retained" = any persisted storage that survives process restarts or is included in backups, snapshots, or long-term logs (e.g., S3 objects, database entries, backups, audit logs stored >24 hours).
- Excluded from "retained" = ephemeral caches, in-memory token/KV caches, and transient GPU memory that are not written to durable storage.

Can you confirm if that language will satisfy Q23 for USmartBank's risk team, or if your reviewers need additional constraints (e.g., specific retention window, encryption-at-rest region asserts, or attestation)?

Next steps we can take if helpful:
- Share a concise evidence packet (dataflow diagram showing region boundaries, retention policy excerpt, SOC 2 control mapping, KMS region table).
- Join a short call to walk through examples (10–20m).

I've attached a first-pass dataflow diagram and an evidence checklist to accelerate the review.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Security & Trust, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-dataflow-diagram.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: sig-evidence-checklist.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@usmartbank.com>

Date: 2027-05-04T12:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: SIG Q23 — Data residency: interpretation for retained vs. transient artifacts

Hi Olga,

Appreciate the proactive note and the diagram. Your proposed interpretation looks reasonable from a first read, but USmartBank's reviewers want to be explicit about two things before we mark Q23 as "Yes/Compliant":

1) Define the retention boundary: is anything stored >24 hours considered "retained"? Our auditors often use the 24-hour threshold but some teams use 7 days.
2) Confirm where persisted logs and backups are physically stored (region) and whether those artifacts can be restored into a different region during DR testing.

Can we do a 20-minute call tomorrow (Wed 5/5) at 10:00 AM ET to go over examples? If you prefer, Neha can send a short follow-up email that lays out the accepted definition and the specific evidence bundle we'll provide.

Thanks,
Jordan Price
Senior InfoSec Manager — USmartBank
security@usmartbank.com

Date: 2027-05-04T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG Q23 — Data residency: interpretation for retained vs. transient artifacts

Jordan / Megan — great, thanks for the quick response. Confirming we'll take the call tomorrow at 10:00 AM ET (Olga & I will join).

To make the call efficient, here is the Redwood position and the evidence we plan to provide:

Redwood Q23 interpretation (proposed definitive wording):
- "Retained" refers to artifacts persisted to durable storage that survive process restarts or are captured in backups/snapshots/audit logs. Specifically included: object storage (S3) blobs, database records, managed audit logs, and scheduled backups/snapshots.
- "Not retained": in-memory buffers, ephemeral KV caches (LRU caches, local GPU KV cache), and transient streaming buffers that are not persisted to durable storage.
- Retention threshold: for the purposes of the SIG, Redwood will treat any artifact retained >= 24 hours as a persisted artifact and therefore within the scope of Q23.

Planned evidence bundle (to be uploaded after the call):
- Dataflow diagram showing region boundaries and storage tiers [redwood-dataflow-diagram.pdf]
- Retention policy excerpt (section: Logs and Backups) [sig-evidence-checklist.xlsx -> tab: retention]
- KMS region mapping table (keys and primary region)
- SOC 2 control mapping excerpt (CC6/CC7 relevance)

If that language looks acceptable on the call we'll send a one-paragraph attestation and the documents above.

Quick calendar link (internal): https://calendar.google.com/event?id=abc123

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head, Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@usmartbank.com>

Date: 2027-05-05T10:01:00-04:00
Subject: Re: SIG Q23 — Data residency: interpretation for retained vs. transient artifacts

Thanks for the call — that was helpful. Agreed items / notes: 

- Agreement in principle: USmartBank will accept the Redwood definition where "retained" = persisted artifacts (>=24 hours) and ephemeral caches are excluded.
- Confirmation needed: persisted backups and long-term logs are stored in the region specified in the contract; DR testing may temporarily spin up restore instances in a DR region but backups remain encrypted and contain metadata indicating origin region.
- Follow-up request: please send a short attestation (1–2 paragraphs) that states the interpretation, references the retention threshold (>=24 hours), and lists the evidence attachments. Our compliance team will accept that as part of the SIG evidence packet.

I've attached a brief set of call notes for your reference.

Jordan

Jordan / Megan,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Per our discussion, please find the agreed-upon attestation and the evidence bundle attached. If your compliance team needs a signed letter on company letterhead we can produce that as a next step.

Redwood attestation (draft):
"Redwood Inference confirms that, for the purposes of SIG question Q23, the term 'retained' refers to artifacts persisted to durable storage (e.g., object storage, database records, backups, and managed audit logs) that survive process restarts or are captured in scheduled backups and snapshots. Transient artifacts such as in-memory buffers, ephemeral KV caches, and GPU-resident token caches that are not written to durable storage are excluded from 'retained.' For SIG scope, Redwood treats artifacts retained for 24 hours or longer as persisted artifacts. Persisted backups and long-term logs for USmartBank customer data are stored in the region specified in the customer's contract; during authorized DR testing, restores may be executed in a DR region while maintaining encryption and origin-region metadata."
Attachments included:
- redwood-dataflow-diagram.pdf (dataflow and storage tiers)
- sig-evidence-checklist.xlsx (retention excerpt; KMS mapping)
